    - Oh! *Player*! Look, up there, just beside the ridge. No, you can't see it in daylight. But it's there. Come back tonight and I'll show you. Five years here and I'm still not tired of this sky.
    - You saw it too. Low toward the island's heart, wavering as if through heat, on a cold still night. I've written the date in the book. I write them all down. I don't know what else to do.
    - Ahvi has the book now, with Skarra's dots set against every date. I came here to study stars, not to frighten anyone. I still don't know what the shimmer is. Nobody does.

    - Ask me about anything. Especially stars.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?

    - Imre, stargazer. I grew up in the lowlands and learned the stars from the old tables in Selsior's Scholars' Quarter. I lodge above Corwell's storeroom and pay in star charts. Corwell says they're worth more than the rent. Corwell is very kind.
    - I came meaning to stay one summer, five years ago. I reached a Tolmach fire on the canyon road after dark and was given water and a place without a single question. And the stars! Nowhere in the kingdom has a sky like this. I never left.
    - Come up to the high terrace on a clear night. Bring a blanket.
